TECH / STRICT

- HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript only.
- No frameworks.
- No libraries.
- Inline CSS and inline JS.
- Remote images are allowed.
- Must work by opening the file directly in a browser.

Create a visually striking cinematic museum-night website.

The design should feel like:
- luxury museum after dark
- velvet darkness
- golden spotlights
- quiet mystery
- art-house cinema
- premium cultural event

- dark velvet / near-black background
- deep burgundy and midnight navy gradients
- soft spotlight effects
- elegant serif headlines
- modern readable sans-serif body text
- thin gold dividers

- large editorial hero layout
- asymmetric image cards
- glass-like dark panels
- premium ticket cards
- smooth hover states
- scroll reveal animations
- strong typography hierarchy

- Background: `#070506`

TYPOGRAPHY
Use CSS font stacks only:
- Headlines: `Georgia`, `Times New Roman`, serif
- Body: `Inter`, `system-ui`, `Segoe UI`, sans-serif

Visible :focus-visible outlines in gold on all interactive elements. NAVBAR: position sticky top 0, glass background that gains stronger background after scroll (class toggled by JS). Logo text 'ARTIFACT' in serif with gold letter-spacing. Links in order: Program (#program), Artists (#artists), Venue (#venue), Tickets (#tickets), FAQ (#faq). CTA button 'Get Tickets' linking to #tickets. Active nav link state: JS with IntersectionObserver or scroll listener sets aria-current="true" and a gold underline class on the link whose section is in view. Mobile hamburger button (aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-label 'Toggle menu') that opens a full-width dropdown panel below 880px; closes on link click and ESC.

HERO (id=top): full-viewport cinematic section (min-height ~100vh). Background image https://source.unsplash.com/featured/2400x1400?museum,night with object-fit cover, overlaid by dark gradient overlay and a spotlight gradient. Large editorial layout: small eyebrow text 'An After-Hours Museum Experience', large serif h1 'Museum Night, Reimagined', below it event name 'ARTIFACT: Museum Night' in gold serif. Date/time/place line: '18 October 2026', '19:00–02:00', 'The Old Gallery, Warsaw'. Small metadata badges (pill shaped glass badges): 'Ticketed', '7 hours', 'Warsaw', '18+'. Two CTAs: primary button 'Get Tickets' (href #tickets) and secondary button 'Save to Calendar' (triggers ICS download). Keep text readable on image.

CONCEPT (id=concept): short editorial paragraph about a night in the museum where galleries open after dark, plus thin gold divider and 3 feature cards with headings: 'After-hours exhibitions', 'Live performances', 'Guided hidden-room tours' each with a short description and small gold icon (inline SVG). Asymmetric layout.

PROGRAM (id=program): section heading 'Program'. Vertical hour-by-hour timeline with a gold vertical line and dots. 8 items exactly:
19:00 — Doors Open (location tag: Main Hall)
19:30 — Curator Welcome (Rotunda)
20:00 — Hidden Collection Tour (Hidden Rooms)
21:00 — Live Ambient Performance (Atrium)
22:00 — Sculpture Hall Projection (Sculpture Hall)
23:00 — Artist Talk (Lecture Room)
00:00 — Midnight Gallery Walk (Galleries A–C)
01:00 — Closing Sound Session (Courtyard)
Each item: time, title, short description, location tag (pill). Readable on mobile.

ARTISTS (id=artists): heading 'Artists & Speakers'. Exactly 8 cards in a responsive grid with asymmetric accents. Each card: image (loading="lazy", alt text, aspect ratio 4/3), name, role, short teaser, and a 'View details' button (data-artist-index). Use images cycling through these URLs:
1 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?gallery,art
2 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?exhibition,lights
3 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?sculpture,museum
4 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?museum,crowd
5 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?art,installation
6 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?theater,stage
(cards 7 and 8 reuse images 1 and 2). Names/roles, invented fictional: e.g. Elena Varga — Sculptor; Marek Lis — Curator; Ada Nowak — Sound Artist; Tomasz Reed — Lighting Designer; Iga Sokol — Performance Artist; Julian Mora — Film Projectionist; Hanna Wit — Archivist; Piotr Dalton — Composer. Each with a teaser and a 'session time' (e.g. 20:00, 22:00, 23:00, 01:00).

ARTIST MODAL: accessible dialog (role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby), focus moved into modal on open, focus trapped with Tab/Shift+Tab, focus restored to trigger on close. Content: image, name, role, longer bio (3-4 sentences), session time, close button (aria-label 'Close'). Closes on ESC, on backdrop click, and on close button. Body scroll locked while open.

VENUE (id=venue): heading 'Venue'. Venue name 'The Old Gallery', address 'ul. Przykładowa 12, 00-001 Warsaw, Poland' (fictional), travel tips, accessibility notes (step-free entrance, accessible restrooms, assistance dogs welcome), parking / public transport notes (metro line and bus stop mention, paid parking nearby). Inline SVG map mock (viewBox, width 100%): dark background, gallery block rectangle with label 'THE OLD GALLERY', several nearby street lines in muted color, a metro/bus marker (circle with 'M' or bus icon), an entrance marker (gold pin), and a gold dashed route line between marker and entrance.

TICKETS (id=tickets): heading 'Tickets'. 3 premium ticket cards:
- Night Pass, €29, bullets: Entry after 19:00; Main exhibition access; Program access
- Curator Pass, €59 (RECOMMENDED badge), bullets: Everything in Night Pass; Hidden collection tour; Reserved artist talk seating
- Patron Pass, €129, bullets: Everything in Curator Pass; VIP lounge access; Signed event print; Priority entrance
Each card has a 'Select tier' button (data-tier), hover highlight. Clicking opens the checkout modal with that tier preselected.

CHECKOUT MODAL (accessible dialog, same focus trap/ESC/backdrop behaviour): shows selected tier (select element to change tier), attendee name input (required, min 2 chars), email input (required, valid email regex), number of tickets (number input 1–10, default 1), computed total price (tier price × quantity, updated live, formatted €), terms checkbox (required), a note 'Demo only — no real payment is processed', and 'Confirm reservation' submit button. Inline validation: each field shows an error message below it with aria-describedby and aria-invalid; errors are shown on submit and on blur. On valid submit: close modal, show success toast 'Reservation confirmed for <name>. Check your inbox (demo).', reset form.

FAQ (id=faq): heading 'FAQ'. Accessible accordion (buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls, panels with hidden attribute, smooth height/opacity animation, only one open at a time optional). At least 6 items:
1. Is payment processed on this page? — No. This is a demo landing page; the checkout is a mock and no real payment is taken.
2. Can I arrive late? — Yes, entry is open from 19:00 until 00:00; after midnight, entry is only through the Midnight Gallery Walk.
3. Are photos allowed? — Photography without flash is allowed in all galleries; tripods and professional equipment require prior approval.
4. Is the venue accessible? — Yes, the venue has a step-free entrance, accessible restrooms, and quiet zones; contact us for specific needs.
5. Can I change my ticket tier? — Yes, tier changes are possible up to 7 days before the event via the confirmation email (demo).
6. How do I save the event to my calendar? — Use the 'Save to Calendar' button to download an .ics file that works with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, and Outlook.

NEWSLETTER (id=newsletter): heading, short text, email input (label, aria), submit button 'Subscribe'. Inline validation with error message on invalid email (regex), success clears input and shows toast 'Thanks for subscribing — see you in the gallery.'

FOOTER: ARTIFACT logo, event credits (Curated by ARTIFACT Collective; Lighting & Sound: Night Studio; Photography: demo credits), social-style text links (Instagram, Facebook, Newsletter — href='#' with aria labels), copyright '© 2026 ARTIFACT: Museum Night', and small note 'Demo landing page — no real ticket purchase.'

SAVE TO CALENDAR (JS): function that builds an ICS string with CRLF line endings: BEGIN:VCALENDAR, VERSION:2.0, PRODID:-//ARTIFACT//Museum Night//EN, CALSCALE:GREGORIAN, METHOD:PUBLISH, BEGIN:VEVENT, UID (unique string), DTSTAMP (current UTC in YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ), DTSTART:20261018T190000, DTEND:20261019T020000, SUMMARY:ARTIFACT: Museum Night, LOCATION:The Old Gallery\, Warsaw (escaped comma), DESCRIPTION:A cinematic after-hours museum event with exhibitions\, performances\, talks\, and guided tours. (escape commas), END:VEVENT, END:VCALENDAR. Create Blob type 'text/calendar;charset=utf-8', URL.createObjectURL, temporary <a download="artifact-museum-night.ics"> clicked then removed, and revoke the object URL after a timeout. Both 'Save to Calendar' buttons (hero and footer/ concept) use this. Show toast 'Calendar file downloaded'.

TOAST: fixed container bottom-right (bottom-center on mobile), aria-live="polite", toasts auto-dismiss after ~4 seconds, slide-in animation, gold border glass style, types success/info/error. Function showToast(message, type).

JS BEHAVIOUR SUMMARY: wrap everything in an IIFE or DOMContentLoaded handler; no console errors (guard all querySelector results); smooth scrolling for nav links via CSS and JS close of mobile menu; active nav state; sticky nav background on scroll; scroll reveal via IntersectionObserver; artist modal data array with bios; ticket tier data array {name, price, recommended}; checkout validation; FAQ accordion; newsletter validation; ICS download; toast; ESC closes any open modal or mobile menu.

RESPONSIVE: mobile-first; breakpoints around 880px and 560px; hero text scales with clamp(); grids collapse to one column on mobile; timeline stays readable on small screens; modals scroll internally with max-height 90vh; ticket cards stack.

ACCESSIBILITY: semantic landmarks (header, nav, main, section with aria-labelledby, footer), skip link 'Skip to content', alt text on all images, sufficient color contrast, buttons are <button> elements, links are <a>. prefers-reduced-motion disables animations.

Output the complete file content only (valid HTML, all tags closed, no placeholder comments like TODO, no external resources except the Unsplash images and the Google-free font stacks specified)."}
